source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Only pregnancy, ruling out all other possible causes, which understates the range of conditions actually linked to this particular lab finding","B":"A normal finding with no clinical significance, contrary to what this significantly elevated ALP value actually warrants","C":"Liver/biliary or bone conditions, requiring further evaluation, rather than the kidney-only cause the colleague is currently assuming this reflects","D":"Only kidney disease, with no other association, similar to what the colleague is currently assuming about this particular lab value"}}
source_row.rationale: Alkaline phosphatase (ALP) is present in several tissues, and elevation is commonly associated with either liver/biliary tract conditions (such as bile duct obstruction or cholestatic liver disease) or bone conditions (such as periods of active bone growth in children/adolescents, Paget's disease of bone, or certain bone cancers/metastases), requiring further evaluation (sometimes including other tests like GGT to help localize the source, since ALP alone doesn't distinguish between hepatic and bone origin) to determine the specific underlying cause.
source_row.source_detail: Hepatic vs. Bone Sources of Elevated ALP
